text: Honestly floored. This is the horror movie audiences have been asking for for years. Unrelenting, brutal, so original, so genuinely unsettling and creepy that at times you start laughing because your body doesn't even know how to regulate. Inde Navarrette is a revelation. Michael Johnston is incredible too. The strength of the acting elevates the premise so much. At no point did I know what was going to happen next, and with each escalation I was terrified to find out. My already high expectations were surpassed by 10 miles. Just brilliant stuff.

Best horror I've seen in a long time. This movie had so much range, you'd be scared shitless and then laugh the next second. Also I had my biggest jump scare ever which I never really fall for, but I literally flew back in my seat and rocked the whole chair lmao. Major respect to the girl playing Nikki she was phenomenal, and props to the crew and actors for making such a quality movie with a low budget. This really is the best movie I've seen in the past 3 years and I'm usually reluctant to ever say something like that but I'm so impressed, this is a must see!

Perfectly Timed. In my opinion, this was the best horror movie of the last couple of years. Perfectly timed comedy and jump scares. The cast was perfect, especially Inde Navarrette. She played her character perfectly. Again, this is all in my opinion, but I really loved it. I had the luck to see this before it was released and I would advise everyone that has the opportunity to go see it. 10/10 Will watch again. :)

8/10 do not recommend. I've watched so many horror movies, from art house to the classics to new ones, and this might be the one that stuck with me the most. I wouldn't say it was the best by any stretch, but it just makes me feel a certain way. It is the most horrifying, devastating, and sad movie I've seen in a long time. I still get nauseous thinking about it. I think this will definitely be the best movie of the last year. High rating but do not recommend to anyone because it made me feel so awful. Also kudos to Inde Navarette! Wow!

Unhinged and thrilling in every way! This movie is, without a doubt, one of the best films I have seen this year. The narrative is easy to follow without being overly complicated, while the atmosphere and tone keep you on the edge of your seat. But beyond these impressive qualities, it is Inde Navarrete's performance that carries the entire film. Through Bear's perspective, you never know what she will do next, while Navarrete completely surrenders herself to the role of Nikki Freeman, creating a character who will be remembered as one of the most compelling in horror. I wouldn't be surprised if Oscar nominations follow, but all I can say is that this is just the beginning for the immensely talented Curry Barker.

Oh my god.... This is a brilliant film. Inde Navarrette's performance is insane and absolutely carried this movie. She definitely deserves the oscar. The film sets up a basic premise and executes it to near perfection. The origins and workings of the one wish willow is probably the only plot hole in this movie I could find. The movie uses creepy and slow burn horror rather than jumpscares which is very effective. The lighting and the cinematography is brilliant.

Surprising. The horror genre rarely surprises me anymore, but Obsession managed to do just that. Rather than chasing cheap scares, it builds dread around a haunting idea: sometimes the greatest horror isn't failing to achieve your lifelong dream, but finally attaining it only to watch it transform into your worst nightmare before your eyes.

Am I getting too old? WHAT was that dialogue? I love horror, I love Indy horror, I love Blumhouse. But seriously, I don't remember that kind of talk even in Jr. High let alone supposed adults who all seem to have their own homes despite their careers of working in a music shop. Do you like me? Do you like like me? So the higher rating is for some of the shots and the ending and some for just what could have been but I did have to use my own brain to fill in the gaps. But the beginning, I tried a rewatch but just can't make it through that crap again.

Overrated. While the movie is watchable, it suffers from too much weirdness and none of the the teased ideas and threads ending up going anywhere. Just a really lazy movie, opening up a bunch of themes and then just buggering off before ANY of them "pay out" at all. Also the rules of the universe make little sense, rhyme or reason. What's behind it? What's going on? - Who cares, let's get this movie over with...

OVERRATED. This movie isn't bad, I love horror and saw this in theaters asap. It's a decent movie but to call this one of the greatest horror movies in recent time is insane. People saying that this movie left them jaw dropped and that it's soooo good is a crazy take. This movie has a great Jumpscare, a decent plot, okay acting with the main character having great acting, the ending was decent, overall just a decent movie I'd rate it no higher than a 6.5 if you think this is a 10 then idk.

Where do I start? I wanted to like this movie, I really did. In stead, I left the cinema needing a xanex because I felt so rattled. The actors were great and pretty believable but the story or something similar has been done many times. Be careful what you wish for because you might just get it... Dire consequences included. For me, there were just too many plot holes to enjoy it much. The ending was just bleak to put it mildly. Without adding spoilers, the whole situation could have been resolved so easily. "Hey, for shits and grins to a rando on the streets I'll give you $50 to break this stick and make one wish!!" But that would have made too much sense to put into a movie that was this clumsy. Wait for streaming and maybe your senses won't be assaulted buy the MUCH too loud background noises in the cinema plex. Don't say I didn't warn you.

unrealistic acting. Obsession has been getting massive praise online as one of the best horror movies recently. But honestly, if this is the standard for great cinema, the art of moviemaking is in trouble. While the whole story feels pretty annoying from start to finish, what really ruins the movie is the unrealistic acting of the male lead. He is completely disconnected from reality and acts so unnaturally that he is impossible to take seriously. Instead of feeling suspense or caring about what happens to him, watching him is just frustrating. In the end, all the high ratings and glowing reviews online can't be anything other than overhyped internet buzz. Obsession proves that viral success doesn't equal good art.

I don't get the OBSESSION! Honestly I don't understand the hype. I felt the movie was repitive and predictable, with very little risk taken. The color was desaturated to the point it felt like a mistake. The writing was uninspired. It leaned way too hard on the in and out of reality displayed by Nikki, which was uninteresting and overdone. You could literally time a jump scare. The acting was okay, but the characters were all unrealistic. For a director's first film it was as expected, a bit messy and low budget. In regard to the hype and high ratings it makes no sense and starts to feel like a TikTok meme caught fire.

Predictable, Annoying, and Overrated. The movie was uninspiring,L and highly predictable. Within the first 5 minutes, you'll know exactly what the movie is about and how it'll end; trust your gut and stop watching. The acting was poor (although how could it not be with such an uninspiring script). By the end of the movie, I was tired of the screaming and gratuitous violent/bloody scenes. It could've been a modern horror of Romeo and Juliet. Instead, it sits among the many other cliche horrors that doesn't illicit anything out of the audience except an occasional shock. Lame.

Dark Romance But the Only Dark Thing Was My Will to Finish This Film. Ah yes, the classic love story. Boy meets girl, mysterious stick appears from absolutely nowhere, chaos ensues, nothing is explained, credits roll. The romantic tension was so dark I genuinely could not see what was happening, emotionally or literally. The fantasies had zero connection to each other. I kept waiting for a plot. It never came. The wish stick has more character development than anyone in this film.

I don't get the high reviews. I don't understand the high reviews for the film, but the movie's story is pretty much in the trailer. There is not much more to it and it is stretched into a 100 minutes filled with cringe. There isn't much character development or world building that gives depth to the film and the acting was mediocre at best. A 2/10 might be harsh but with such high expectations after seeing the high scores I was very disappointed.

Overrated. Weirdly overrated! It's more like a psychological comedy rather than a horror movie. Not even close to 5. The movie lack the element of surprise. In addition, all horror scenes are very surfacial and extremely brief. It's a total waste of time. I am starting to think twice about trusting the imdb scores anymore.

I tried really hard to like this.... For about 15 minutes and then realized I should not have to try. If the creators of this film set out to make a movie that would make me feel bored, insulted and disappointed... then it was a success.. Complete Garbage. I am a huge fan of horror and this looked and felt like a Shudder bottom bin feature with 3.6 stars. Apologies to the hard working crew and artists that worked on this film. And another thing- STOP comparing this to Weapons. Not even close. In your dreams, Curry.

Amazing Journey! Horror of the good old days. Must See for every Horror lover. Watched it in Dolby Atmos and it was absolute Worth it. Dont Look on the Bad Reviews here. Some people cant be happy with all. Not a videogame anymore at all, but loved every Second of This Movie. Last year weapons has been amazing and now This. Give it a try. Best October Movie so far!

text: Beat movie. I have never submitted a review before in my entire life, and I am specifically writing this one to express my support for everyone who was involved in creating this movie. This is truly the finest film I have ever experienced while watching with a group of people; excellent job, as I genuinely found this movie to be thoroughly enjoyable. My hope is that we will see more movies of this caliber released in the future.

The best 10/10. This is amazing. It's the best Resident Evil movie. The special effects, the story, the atmosphere... everything is so good. You really get immersed in the story and drama, and it makes you feel like you're actually inside the video game. The protagonist is perfect because he's just a normal person, and that makes you feel like you're experiencing everything alongside him, or even like you are him.

As a Resident Evil games player since RE1, I approve this movie 10/10. Finally, a Resident Evil movie that captures the same suspense and thrill we felt while playing the early games (especially RE1 and RE2), while delivering the advanced mutated villains of RE4. It hooks you right from the start and gives you almost no time to relax. The film throws you into a frantic race to complete a mission, only to keep slamming into trouble along the way: the first zombie encounter, getting stopped by police, grabbing that initial handgun with limited ammo, getting chased by a mutated dog, and more. The tunnel scene in particular was brilliant. The camera angles are brilliantly game-like, and the environment lighting and score are perfectly on point.

Exactly what i wanted from the movie. So, it excels in certain areas (comedy, tension, body horror, linear narrative), but personally, I felt it lost points on dialogue and the plausibility of the secondary characters. It's very enjoyable and also features some sadder sequences, blending comedy and drama quite well. The ending is really good and captures a perspective I haven't seen before in zombie or infected movies.

Not what you expect. As a fan of the games, I was not expecting the comedy-horror dynamic this strikes. It's very unique...unlike any other horror I've seen. You go from laughing out loud to screaming with classic resident evil jump scares. There's a couple of Easter eggs for us gamers, but nothing too crazy. It strays from the games story a bit, but still stands on its own as a fun story in the resident evil universe.

Fun, creepy and surprisingly funny but the end.... Honestly, I really enjoyed this. It was a good *Resident Evil* movie and had a nice mix of horror, action, and even some moments that were genuinely funny. I wasn't expecting to laugh as much as I did. The atmosphere was great, and there were some really fun moments throughout. My only problem was the ending. It felt a little rushed and kind of left me wanting more, like there should've been another 10-15 minutes to properly finish everything. Still, I had a great time watching it. 8/10 - really fun, creepy, and definitely worth watching.

Good to be back. This should be what an RE movie look like, i mean its first outbreak you guys dont know what to do with virus spread around you, and yet only some people are survive, of course they are umbrella employee. The main char did it well too with some experince he had while he sending package, and the most funny moment when zombie in elevator spit him, omfg that so hillarious. Sad moment the ending was not so well.

A lot of fun but held back by a frustrating ending. I thought the movie was a good time. Austin Abrams is great in the lead. The body horror is fantastic. There are a lot of jumpscares, but they feel earned. Most of the jokes landed, but I thought they could have cut a few of the silly one liners from Abram's character. My biggest issue by far was the ending. I found it abrupt, frustrating, and unsatisfying. Kinda left a sour taste in my mouth, but I did still enjoy the movie.

Really? 10/10? Some people must be very easy to please to think this movie is a perfect 10 out of 10. It's not that good. It's not a bad movie, at least it kinda feels similar to the early games. But I give it a 6. Much room for improvement but not all that bad. An average horror movie, with plenty of humour. Could have been so much more.

P to it, like "THE THING" Spin off or something, but they landed on "RESIDENT EVIL MOVIE" for the I. P they wanted to use.

Nothing like the games disgrace to Resident evil. As an OG Resident Evil fan, I love the games so much. There are all timers to me. The movie is too comedic; the zombies felt unrealistic at times, and the lack of gun use didn't make me feel like I'm playing the games. You just have him shooting a bunch at locks instead of zombies. Sad. Resident Evil is based on action horror; this movie just heavily relies only on jump scares. Which just makes it another horror movie. This is a disgrace to Re.

It has nothing to do with the Resident Evil ga. If it had been released under a different name, I would be watching it with enjoyment right now. A lot of money was spent on the advertising campaign. As if it were going to surpass *Obsession*-in the horror genre? Give me a break!

If you liked the first movie, you will love this one! This movie was just as exciting as the first movie and keeps you interested throughout the whole movie. Film first, read it later! As a big fan of the excellent book this is based on, I was very excited for the film. It's stunning to look at, well acted, skillfully directed and as short as it can be - so certainly worth seeing in IMAX. But buy the book on the way home. Trust me ;)

Earnestness is a Virtue. It's so refreshing to see a well made sci fi movie that completely leans into its premise and trusts its audience to follow its wavelength. I don't like praising a movie for what it's not, but the total lack of cynicism is one of its biggest strengths. More importantly, it's a fully realized story with compelling characters who feel realistic and human, even though one of them is about as far from human as movie aliens get. Consider me pleasantly surprised.

Skimps on the science of the book but delivers the heart. I have read the book and the audiobook. Both are superb. There is a lot missing from the original text but the film distills the essence down to the most important thing; the heart of relationship between Rocky and Grace. The movie is well made but I didn't like the out of focus periphery which became irksome after a while. Other than that, a fantastic effort. A must see and quite moving.

Genre-Defying Heart. I knew this film was about a guy in space on a 'Hail Mary' mission. That's it. So I expected a slow paced, serious space film as many of them are. What I got was a film that moves at a steady pace and has a range of emotions from laughter to sadness. It's quite long at 2.5 hours, but they reduce space fatigue for the audience by using flashbacks to fill in the story. Should I Watch it? Yes.

What is the hype all about ? Dont get me wrong, it is a very watchable fun movie. But i am ver surprised by alot of people calling it the best thing since sliced bread. What am i missing here ? Over hyped. I'm glad I read the book first. It did everything better. More mystery, more tension, more problem solving, and better relationships between the characters. Too long for such a simple plot. A simple plot like this did not need a 2.5h movie. It seems like story telling has become a lost art these days in Hollywood. The movie was going back and forth between the present and the past slowly reveling the reason the lead was out in space, which most had probably figured out after 40min. This movie felt extremely dragged out and could have been wrapped up in under 2 hours.

Disappointing. First of all, those who are comparing this to Interstellar or Martian need to get a mental check-up. Not that this movie is bad but it should be marketed as a kids/ Disney movie. Difficult to review. I am torn about how I felt about this movie. On the one hand, I really liked how the filmmakers were able to get you to sympathize with an animated robot and really root for him. This was very well done, and much of the animation was stunning. In many ways, this was a very impressive effort. However, I also found the film to be excruciatingly slow at certain points. It seemed as if the filmmaker felt that the audience was too stupid to make inferences about the characters unless he drew scenes out for a very long time and beat them over the head with it. I found myself becoming increasingly bored as the movie wore on. If it had been edited down 30 minutes, it would have been a much better movie.
